About Advanced Academic Programs
Advanced Academic Programs (AAP) is a Johns Hopkins University’s
Krieger School of Arts and Sciences division. As part of the
nation’s first research university, AAP offers rigorous and
high-quality master’s degrees at the Hopkins Bloomberg Center in
Washington, DC, at the Homewood campus in Baltimore, Maryland, and
online. AAP distinguishes itself through its intensive
instructional assistance, selective admissions, over 60 dedicated
full-time faculty. Tenured Krieger School faculty members serve as
program chairs to oversee the academic rigor of AAP’s graduate
offerings. For more information, please see http://advanced.jhu.edu/ .

Position Description The MS in Financial Economics
program at Johns Hopkins University is seeking applications to
establish a pool of qualified adjunct instructors for future
teaching opportunities. While appointments are based on program
needs, we anticipate hiring additional adjunct faculty in upcoming
semesters.

We are particularly interested in instructors qualified to teach
one or more of the following courses:

Financial Economics
Financial Econometrics
Financial Intermediation and Financial Markets
Economics of Investments and Financial Management
Behavioral Economics and Finance
Economics of Derivatives
Other graduate-level finance and economics courses aligned with
the program curriculum

The ideal candidate has a passion for graduate education and its
power to transform the careers of working professionals,
international students, and nontraditional learners. Successful
candidates will have a demonstrated record of effective graduate
(in-person and/or online) teaching and a commitment to creating an
engaging and inclusive learning environment.

As the finance profession continues to evolve with advances in
artificial intelligence and data analytics, we are especially
interested in instructors who can thoughtfully incorporate AI tools
and AI-related skills into their teaching where appropriate.
Examples include using AI to support financial analysis, data
visualization, programming, forecasting, risk analysis, investment
research, and decision-making, while also helping students
understand the opportunities and limitations of these
technologies.

The expected salary range for this position is: $8,755 - $9,270 per
course.

The referenced salary range is based on Johns Hopkins
University's good faith belief at the time of posting. The actual
compensation offered to the selected candidate may vary and will be
based on factors including, but not limited to, the experience and
qualifications of the selected candidate – e.g., years in rank,
training, field, discipline, other work experience, and other
similar factors; geographic location; internal equity; external
market conditions; and other factors as reasonably determined by
the University.

Qualifications

Minimum Qualifications

Master's degree in Economics, Finance, or a closely related
field.
At least one year of graduate-level teaching experience
(in-person, online, or hybrid).
At least one year of relevant professional experience in
economics, finance, banking, investments, risk management, or a
related field.

Preferred Qualifications

Ph.D. in Economics, Finance, or a closely related field.
Several years of graduate-level teaching experience.
Significant industry experience in finance or economics.
Experience integrating AI tools, data analytics, programming,
or other emerging technologies into finance or economics
instruction.
Experience designing applied learning activities that connect
theory with current industry practice.

Application Instructions

The position will remain open until it is filled. Candidates must
submit the following:

Cover letter
CV
Teaching evaluations for the three most recently taught
course
Teaching statement (1–2 pages) describing how to incorporate AI
into a graduate finance course.

The following additional vaccine requirements may apply,
depending upon your campus. Please contact the hiring department

The pre-employment physical for positions in clinical areas,
laboratories, working with research subjects, or involving
community contact requires documentation of immune status against
Rubella (German measles), Rubeola (Measles), Mumps, Varicella
(chickenpox), Hepatitis B and documentation of having received the
Tdap (Tetanus, diphtheria, pertussis) vaccination. This may include

vaccines; or antibody status to these diseases from laboratory

ordinarily included in the pre-employment physical exam except for

vaccinations required for these diseases will be given at no cost
in our Occupational Health office.
